chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you seeks a need, let him praise his Lord and extol Him, for when a man seeks a need from a ruler, he prepares for him the best speech he is able to muster.'

So when you seek a need, glorify Allah, the Mighty, the Compeller, and praise Him and extol Him, saying: 'O the Most Generous of those who give, and O the Best of those who are asked, O the Most Merciful of those who are shown mercy, O the One, O the Eternal, O He who did not beget nor was begotten, and there is none comparable to Him, O He who took no companion and no son, O He who does what He wills and decrees what He desires and ordains what He loves, O He who turns between a man and his heart, O He who is at the Exalted View, O He who is like nothing else, O the All-Hearing, O the All-Seeing!'

And frequent the Names of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for the Names of Allah are many, and send blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny, and say: 'O Allah, expand upon me from Your permissible sustenance that which I can suffice with, and repay with regarding my trust, and connect with my kinship, and it be a help to me in Hajj and Umrah.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'A man entered the mosque, prayed two cycles, then asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Then another came, prayed two cycles, then praised Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and sent blessings upon the Prophet and his Progeny. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette and formula for making a supplication in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the principle of *al-hamd* (praise) and *al-du'a* (supplication) as a structured protocol, drawing an analogy to courtly etiquette where one prepares eloquent praise before making a request to a sovereign. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on utilizing the Beautiful Names (*Asma al-Husna*) to align the supplicant’s heart with divine attributes before asking, thereby transforming the act of asking into an act of worship. The concluding narrative reinforces that hastiness in petitioning is less effective than first establishing a spiritual connection through glorification and blessings upon the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ays Bin Al Qasim who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever one of you seek the need, so let him Laud upon His<sup>azwj</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and let him Praise Him<sup>azwj</sup>, for whenever the man seeks the need from a ruling authority, he prepares the speech for him as best as he is able to.

So whenever you seek the need, so Glorify Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Mighty, the Compeller, and Praise Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and Laud upon Him<sup>azwj</sup>. You should be saying, 
‘O the most Benevolent of the ones who give, and O the best of the ones asked from, O the most Merciful of the one who are merciful, O the One, O Last, O the One Who does not beget nor is begotten and there is no one a match for Him<sup>azwj</sup>, O the One who neither took a female companion nor a son, O the One who Does whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to and Decides whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Wants to and Ordains whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> Loves, O the One who Turns around between the man and his heart, O the One Who is at the Exalted viewpoint, O the One Who there is none like Him<sup>azwj</sup>, O the Hearer, O the Seer!’.

And frequent from the Names of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, for the Names of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> are a lot, and send Blessings upon Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and his<sup>saww</sup> Progeny<sup>asws</sup> and say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Expand upon me, from Your<sup>azwj</sup> Grace, the Permissible, what I can suffice with, and can pay back from my entrustments, and help my relatives with it, and it can happen to be a assistance for me regarding the Hajj and the Umrah’’.
And heasws said: ‘A man entered the Masjid, so he prayed two Cycles of Salāt, then asked Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic.
So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The servant was hasty with his Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’.
And another man came over, so he prayed two Cycles of Salāt, then Lauded upon Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic, and sent Blessings upon the Prophetsaww and hissaww Progenyasws.
So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Ask, you will be Given’’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from ‘Iys ibn al-Qasim who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Whenever anyone of you wishes to ask for help he should praise his Lord and thank Him. When a man wants to ask a king for something, he prepares to say the best of words that he can.

When you like to ask for help, speak of the Glory of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Compelling, thank Him and praise Him saying, “O the Most Generous in granting favors and the Best to be asked for help. O the Most Kind to those who ask for kindness, O the only One and Self-sufficient. O the One Who has no children and is not born from anyone and there is no one as His partner. O the One Who has no companion and children. O the One Who does as He wishes, commands as He wills and judges as He loves. O the One Who stands between a man and his heart, O the One Who is in a high position, O the One in Whose likeness there is no creature, O the Hearing, and the Seeing.”

Speak of the names of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy; they are many and ask from Him favors for Muhammad and his family and then say, ‘O Lord, extend for me of Your lawful supplies with which I can save my face, return safely what is entrusted with me, maintain good relations with relatives and be helpful in my Hajj and ‘Umrah.’

The Imam said, ‘Once a man came in the Mosque, performed two Rak’at (prayer consisting of twice kneeling) then asked Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, for help and the Messenger of Allah said, ‘The servant (of Allah) hastened his Lord.’

n another man came in and prayed two Rak’at then he praised Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, and asked from Him favors for the Holy Prophet and his family and the Messenger of Allah said, ‘Ask for help you will receive it.’”
